editorial:
Imagine you are stepping onto a fancy, old-school train for a trip back to London. You get to meet Hercule Poirot, the world's smartest detective, who is just trying to relax after a long job in Istanbul. Everything seems great until a rock slide stops the train in its tracks. Suddenly, a mean businessman is found dead in his room with nine stab wounds. Since the train is stuck in the snow and no one could have left, you know the killer is sitting right there in the dining car with everyone else. It creates a tense, mysterious mood where you start questioning every single passenger.

You will love how the movie builds the mystery piece by piece. The acting is solid, and the plot twists keep you guessing until the very end. While it is a TV movie and does not have huge action scenes, the dialogue keeps things moving fast. If you enjoy puzzles, you should definitely check this out.
endingExplained: Poirot discovers that the victim was actually a kidnapper who killed a little girl years ago. He finds out that all twelve passengers were connected to that family. Instead of one person doing it, every single passenger took turns stabbing the man to get revenge. Poirot gives the police a fake story saying a stranger did it, letting the passengers go free because he feels the man deserved to die.
targetAudience: Ideal for anyone who loves a good whodunit puzzle.
